Energy Fuels is a high-priority underfollowed follow-up because the market may still categorize it as uranium while its rare-earth oxide and heavy-REE separation progress could matter if feedstock provenance becomes the binding constraint.

USA Rare Earth is a direct but execution-sensitive candidate; monitor whether Stillwater and LCM convert nominal capacity into commercial and defense-qualified non-Chinese-feedstock magnet-chain output.
NioCorp belongs in a speculative shadow list, not the core direct list, until evidence improves on financing, construction, separated magnetic-REE output, and magnet-customer qualification.
For this node, the key gating question is not only rare-earth resource ownership but proof of compliant oxide-to-metal-to-alloy-to-magnet qualification for defense or defense-adjacent customers.

Need a later pass on non-US primary listings and ADR/OTC names such as Lynas and Neo Performance, plus private magnet makers such as Vulcan Elements, because US-listed-only screening may miss actual qualified capacity.

MP remains the reference anchor for US mine-to-magnet integration, but its high attention level makes it less useful for the underfollowed lane except as a benchmark for qualification, capacity, and feedstock compliance.

Energy Fuels should be tracked as a heavy-rare-earth oxide bottleneck candidate rather than only as a uranium name; key survival test is repeated Dy/Tb magnet qualification and commercial-scale non-Chinese feedstock.

Neo Performance Materials is a strong underfollowed OTC/Canadian-listed allied magnet-chain candidate because it combines Estonia separation, heavy REE work, magnetic materials, and permanent magnet qualification milestones.

Critical Metals is a speculative-shadow upstream feedstock candidate; keep only if later evidence shows viable processing, financing, offtake, and qualification into Western oxide or magnet supply chains.

For this node, the highest-value evidence is not mining resource size alone; it is proof of non-Chinese feedstock origin, separated NdPr/Dy/Tb oxide quality, metal/alloy conversion, magnet production, and customer or defense-prime qualification.

Need a later pass on private and non-US-listed chokepoints such as USA Rare Earth, Vulcan Elements, Lynas, VAC, Arnold Magnetic, REalloys, and alloy/metallization equipment vendors; they may explain which public names receive offtake or toll-processing demand.
MP should remain the reference anchor for U.S. rare-earth magnet policy support, but it is not the main underfollowed lane because market attention and DoD linkage are already high.
Energy Fuels is a stronger underfollowed candidate than generic rare-earth miners because its relevance is tied to separated NdPr and Dy oxide qualification for permanent magnets.

USA Rare Earth should be tracked as a midstream-plus-downstream candidate: LCM metal/alloy/strip casting and Stillwater magnet manufacturing may be more important than Round Top mining optionality in this node.

Ucore is a speculative shadow candidate because it targets the separation/refining bottleneck with DoD-backed RapidSX work, but survival in later layers depends on commercial commissioning, qualified feedstock, and magnet-maker offtakes.
For this node, separate headline mine ownership from qualified oxide, metal/alloy, strip-cast alloy, magnet production, defense-prime qualification, and feedstock provenance.
Next layer should test whether candidates have actual defense-compliant qualification and binding customer demand, not just domestic capacity announcements or generic critical-minerals exposure.

USAR belongs in the underfollowed lane because its Stillwater magnet commissioning and LCM alloy capability map directly to the oxide-to-alloy-to-magnet chokepoint.
UUUU is a second-order feedstock/oxide qualification candidate; its uranium label may hide rare-earth oxide optionality tied to non-Chinese NdPr, Dy, and Tb supply.
NB is a speculative shadow candidate only; rare-earth production remains optional and should be falsified if no feasibility update, financing, or offtake emerges.
For this node, qualification status and feedstock origin should be treated as more important than headline mine resources or nominal magnet capacity.

Need later-layer verification of defense-prime qualification, waiver timelines, non-Chinese chain-of-custody documentation, and whether private magnet makers such as Vulcan convert oxide validation into binding long-term offtakes with public suppliers.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct US-listed universe around the rare-earth magnet and non-Chinese-feedstock qualification node. The strongest direct reference anchor is MP Materials, which now spans mining, separation, metal/alloy, and magnet manufacturing. The underfollowed lane includes Energy Fuels as a US rare-earth oxide processor with NdPr and heavy-REE oxide relevance, USA Rare Earth as a newly public integrated mine-to-magnet developer with Stillwater magnet capacity and LCM alloy exposure, and NioCorp as a speculative small-cap upstream critical-minerals developer with magnetic rare-earth optionality but weaker current magnet-chain qualification evidence. Key falsification risk: nominal ex-China capacity may not translate into defense-qualified, non-Chinese-feedstock-compliant supply. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the chokepoint hypothesis that defense-relevant rare-earth magnet exposure is less about headline mine ownership and more about qualified non-Chinese oxide, heavy rare earth, metal/alloy, and magnet-chain capacity. The pass keeps MP Materials as the obvious reference anchor, then prioritizes underfollowed or narrower public names tied to separated oxides, heavy rare earths, European/Western magnet conversion, and future non-Chinese feedstock qualification. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
